name: colWeightedMedians
title: Calculates the weighted medians for each column in a matrix

origin.description: Calculates the weighted medians for each row (column) in a matrix.
origin.usage:
colWeightedMedians(x, w = NULL, rows = NULL, cols = NULL,
  na.rm = FALSE, ..., useNames = TRUE)

arguments.name: w
arguments.text: A numeric vector of length N (one weight per row).

arguments.name: rows
arguments.text: A vector indicating a subset of rows to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: cols
arguments.text: A vector indicating a subset of columns to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: na.rm
arguments.text: If TRUE, missing values are excluded.

arguments.name: useNames
arguments.text: If TRUE (default), names attributes of the result are set, otherwise not.

origin.details: If no weights are given, colMedians() is used. Otherwise each column is passed to weightedMedian() after base-R subscripting. A negative weight is an error. w is subset by rows, and its length is checked against the original number of rows.
origin.value: A numeric vector of length K (one value for each selected column).

translation.description: Calculates the weighted medians for each row (column) in a matrix.
translation.usage:
colWeightedMedians(x, w=None, rows=None, cols=None, na_rm=False,
  use_names=True, interpolate=None, ties=None, idxs=None)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An N by K array. Axis 0 is rows and axis 1 is columns, matching the printed R matrix. A one-dimensional sequence is rejected.

arguments.name: w
arguments.text: A numeric vector of length N, one weight per row. None uses the unweighted median. A negative weight is an error. Zero is passed on and dropped by weightedMedian. A missing weight makes every column missing when na_rm is false.

arguments.name: rows
arguments.text: 1-based rows to include. None uses every row. w is subset with this same index after its length has been checked against the original matrix.

arguments.name: cols
arguments.text: 1-based columns to include. None uses every column. Zero is dropped, a positive index keeps its place and may repeat, and a negative index drops that column.

arguments.name: na_rm
arguments.text: If True, missing values in a column are excluded, and a missing weight is dropped. This is na.rm. The default is False.

arguments.name: use_names
arguments.text: Accepted for compatibility with useNames. The result is always a plain float64 vector; names are not attached.

arguments.name: interpolate
arguments.text: Passed to weightedMedian when w is given. None follows that function: true when ties is omitted, false when ties is given. Ignored when w is None.

arguments.name: ties
arguments.text: Passed to weightedMedian when w is given. A positive infinite weight ignores ties. Ignored when w is None.

arguments.name: idxs
arguments.text: 1-based index forwarded to weightedMedian for each column, after rows and cols have been applied. None uses the whole column. Ignored when w is None.

translation.details: With weights, each selected column is passed to weightedMedian together with w, na_rm, interpolate, ties, and idxs. With no weights, the result follows colMedians. An empty column selection returns a zero-length vector. A matrix with no rows and no weights returns plain NaN for each column; the same shape with an empty weight vector returns R's NA for each column.
translation.value: A float64 vector of length K, one value for each selected column.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from matrixstats.rowweightedmedians import colWeightedMedians

x = np.array([[1.0, 5.0, 9.0], [2.0, 6.0, 10.0], [3.0, 7.0, 11.0], [4.0, 8.0, 12.0]])
colWeightedMedians(x, w=np.array([1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0]))
